objectives: Read short controlled sentences containing taught /n/ patterns.
Identify who, action and location details directly stated in a sentence.
Reread after decoding to connect accurate word reading with meaning.
concepts: Sentence comprehension depends on accurate decoding plus meaning-making.
Literal questions can be answered from explicitly stated information.
A single final-sound error can change a word and therefore change sentence meaning.

definitions.definition: Understanding the meaning and explicit information contained in a sentence.
Information directly stated in the text.
Reading the text again to confirm accuracy and meaning.

workedExamples: Nan sat. → Who? Nan. What did Nan do? Sat.
Nan sat at a mat. → Where? At a mat.
If mat is read as map, reread and check the final sound /t/.
commonMistakes: Answering from memory instead of the sentence.
Reading accurately but not checking meaning.
Guessing a word from its first sound.
revisionPoints: Decode → reread → identify detail → answer from text.

higherOrderThinking: Explain why a final-sound error can change meaning.
mixedReview: Decode, reread and answer text-based questions.

mistakeBasedRevision: If a detail is wrong, reread the exact sentence.
If mat/map is confused, isolate the final sound.
weakTopicRevision: Read each sentence twice and point to the word supporting the answer.

activities.name: Evidence pointing
steps: Locate the supporting word or phrase.

outcomes: Learner reads controlled /n/ sentences with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner identifies explicit who/action/location details with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner notices when a decoding error changes sentence meaning.
Learner uses rereading and text evidence to answer comprehension questions.

questions.question: Read: “Nan sat at a mat.” Where did Nan sit?
Read: “Nan sat.” What did Nan do?
Read: “Nan sat at a mat.” What did Nan sit at?
Which sentence tells where Nan sat?
Which word tells who is in the sentence “Nan sat”?
Which word tells the action in “Nan sat”?
Why should the learner reread a sentence after decoding it?
options: To connect the words to meaning

questions.question: A learner reads “Nan sat at a mat” correctly but says Nan sat at a map. What should the learner do?
options: Reread the sentence and check the final sound in mat

questions.question: Which sentence has the same meaning as “Nan sat.”?
What information is directly stated in “Nan sat at a mat”?
Which question checks a sentence detail?
options: How many letters are in Nan?

questions.question: What should an answer to a sentence question be based on?
Which reading behavior supports comprehension?
options: Decode accurately, then reread for meaning

questions.question: What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Read controlled /n/ sentences accurately and understand their stated meaning
